correctness.rationale: Exact exhaustive C++17 enumeration computes all triple atomic diagrams with equality and adjacency for n=1..26, and the independent Python nested-set recursion confirms n=1..12. A separate mathematical 2-endpoint-per-round gap invariant, with t_r=3*t_(r-1)+2, proves equivalence for all n,m>=26. The finite types show precisely classes n=1,2,3,4,5 and n>=6. The boundary G5 vs G6 has a distinct one-vertex two-round type represented by [3,4]. No extrapolation from a finite census is used for the infinite claim.

evidence: Ganian et al., arXiv:1302.6043v4, Section 3, Theorems 4 and 6: generic bounded-rank sparsification/model-checking algorithms for fixed finite interval-length sets.
The complete discrete-interval family has lengths 0 through n-1, not a fixed length set; moreover a decision algorithm by itself does not state the six-class exact cutoff.
The universal 3^q-1 endpoint-game bound is supplied independently in the present proof and gives only 26 when q=3, not the sharp value 6.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The primary interval-graph model-checking theorem is algorithmic and restricted to a fixed set of allowed lengths. It neither states nor logically yields a specific six-parameter-class result without a substantive additional exact finite classification. The general EF characterization is a method, not a dominating parameter theorem.

originality.rationale: Exact comparison of theorem statements and primary-text implications revealed no covering result. Ganian et al. prove an algorithmic model-checking theorem for length-restricted interval graphs, not the six-class depth-three classification of the all-discrete-interval family. Available published result summaries about directed paths, Boolean algebras, and interval containment do not imply this statement in the same signature and rank. This is best-knowledge originality, not a proof of global priority.

value.rationale: The all-contiguous-subinterval family is a canonical, complete interval-graph family with n(n+1)/2 vertices. The theorem gives all exact rank-three classes and a sharp 21-vertex representative bound, improving a general structural 26-endpoint sufficient bound to the actual six-endpoint cutoff. This naturally quantifies the logical visibility of interval intersection without arbitrary slicing or a merely routine number increase.
